qt: An object moves round a circle at a constant speed. In which direction does its acceleration point?
Which force provides the centripetal force in each case? (1) A mass whirled round in a circle on the end of a string. (2) A car rounding a corner on a flat road. (3) The Moon orbiting the Earth.

“Centripetal” means centre-seeking and “centrifugal” means centre-fleeing. In an inertial frame of reference (one in which Newton’s laws hold), which statement about a “centrifugal force” on an object moving in a circle is correct?
Riding in the back seat of a car that turns a corner, you slide across the seat as if pushed outwards, away from the centre of the turn. Which is the correct explanation?

A 0.50 kg mass on a frictionless table is tied to a string that passes through a hole in the centre of the table to a hanging mass. The 0.50 kg mass moves round a circle of radius 0.20 m at 2.3 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it.

The 0.50 kg mass circles at 2.3 m/s on a radius of 0.20 m, held in its circle by a string that runs through the hole in the frictionless table to a hanging mass M, which stays at rest. Calculate M. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A car travelling at 14 m/s goes round an unbanked (flat) bend of radius 96 m. Calculate its centripetal acceleration.

The car goes round the flat bend of radius 96 m at 14 m/s, with sideways friction from the road providing all of the centripetal force. The friction force can be at most μ × (normal contact force), where μ is the coefficient of friction. Calculate the minimum value of μ that lets the car round the bend. Take g = 9.81 m/s².

A mass on a string moves in a vertical circle. T is the tension in the string and mg is the weight of the mass. Which expressions give the resultant (centripetal) force on the mass at the top and at the bottom of the circle?

A 1.7 kg object is swung on the end of a 0.60 m string in a vertical circle, taking 1.1 s for each revolution. Treating its speed as constant, calculate the tension in the string at the top of the circle. Take g = 9.81 m/s².

The same 1.7 kg object on a 0.60 m string goes round its vertical circle once every 1.1 s. Treating its speed as constant, calculate the tension in the string at the bottom of the circle. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A mass on a string is swung in a vertical circle with only just enough speed to keep it moving in the circle. What is the tension in the string when the mass is at the top?
An object is swung in a vertical circle of radius 0.75 m. Calculate the minimum speed it must have at the top of the circle to stay in circular motion. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A car travels at a constant speed round a frictionless banked bend, as shown. Which forces act on the car?
On a frictionless banked bend, what provides the centripetal force on the car?
A bend of radius 475 m is to be banked so that a car can go round it at 22 m/s without needing any friction. Calculate the angle θ at which the road must be banked. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A 0.25 kg toy plane on a string flies round a horizontal circle of radius 0.80 m. The string makes an angle of 28° with the vertical. Calculate the period of the plane’s motion. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
Alice rides in a car on a theme-park ride. The car travels round a circular track that is banked, as shown, and friction is negligible. Which two forces act on the car?
The mass of Alice’s car and its passengers is 9.60 × 10² kg, and the frictionless track is banked at 20° to the horizontal. Calculate the size of the centripetal force on the car. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A 0.250 kg ball on the end of a cord 1.20 m long is swung in a vertical circle. At the position shown its speed is 4.00 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on the ball at this instant.
Why does a ball swung on a cord in a vertical circle move fastest at the bottom of the circle?
The ball is swung in a vertical circle with the cord taut all the way round. How does the tension in the cord at the bottom of the circle compare with the tension at the top?
Compare the centripetal (resultant) force on the ball at the top and at the bottom of its vertical circle.
The 0.250 kg ball is swung in a vertical circle on a cord 1.20 m long. Calculate the minimum speed it must have at the top of the circle for the cord to stay taut. Take g = 9.81 m/s².

The ball has its minimum speed of 3.43 m/s at the top of the circle (cord 1.20 m). Using conservation of energy, calculate the angle θ from the top of the circle — measured at the centre, from the upward vertical — at which the ball’s speed has risen to 4.00 m/s. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
A 1.80 kg bob on a cord 1.55 m long swings as a conical pendulum, moving round a horizontal circle of radius 0.290 m. Calculate the angle θ between the cord and the vertical.
The 1.80 kg bob of a conical pendulum moves round a horizontal circle of radius 0.290 m on a cord 1.55 m long. Calculate the tension in the cord. Take g = 9.81 m/s².
Calculate the speed the 1.80 kg bob must have to move round its horizontal circle of radius 0.290 m on the 1.55 m cord. Take g = 9.81 m/s².

The London Eye is a giant wheel with 32 passenger capsules evenly spaced round its rim. Each capsule has a mass of 1.0 × 10⁴ kg, is 68 m from the centre of the wheel and moves at a constant 0.26 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force that keeps a capsule moving in its vertical circle.
A passenger stands on the floor of a capsule at the position shown, on the side of the turning wheel. Which forces act on her, and how do they give her centripetal force?
Jon spins Ana round a horizontal circle on the ice by holding her arm, as shown. In which direction does the tension force from Jon’s arm act on Ana at the instant shown?

Ana (mass 55 kg) moves round a horizontal circle of radius 0.95 m, and the tension force in Jon’s arm is 5.00 × 10² N. Calculate Ana’s speed, giving your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.
Jan swings a 10 kg iron ball on a steel wire round a horizontal circle, shown from above. In which direction is the ball’s acceleration at the instant shown?
In which direction does the steel wire pull on Jan?
The iron ball moves round its horizontal circle at a constant speed. Why is a horizontal force needed on the ball?
The 10 kg iron ball goes round a horizontal circle of radius 2.0 m, taking 1.5 s for each rotation. Calculate the centripetal force on the ball.
After a few rotations the ball moves round a circle of the same radius, but with a shorter period. What happens to the horizontal force that the wire exerts on Jan?
An 18 kg suitcase rides on a horizontal circular conveyor belt of radius 7.0 m. The unbalanced (resultant) force on it is 5.5 N. Calculate the time the belt takes to complete one rotation.
Jason (mass 65 kg) stands on a merry-go-round, 4.0 m from its centre. The merry-go-round takes 15 s to make a complete turn. Calculate the centripetal force needed to keep him moving in his circle.
Janet’s ball moves round a horizontal circle of radius 0.75 m, taking 0.84 s to go round her head once. Calculate the acceleration of the ball.
Which force makes Janet’s ball accelerate as it goes round its circle, and how does it change the ball’s velocity?
The referee’s 40.0 g whistle moves round a horizontal circle of radius 0.500 m, taking 1.40 s for each rotation. Calculate the horizontal force that the string exerts on the whistle.
Considering the horizontal forces on the whistle, why does it keep moving round its circle at a constant speed?
The speed of the 40.0 g whistle is reduced to 1.0 m/s, still on a circle of radius 0.500 m. Calculate the new horizontal force needed to keep it moving in the circle.
At 1.0 m/s the whistle needs a horizontal force of only 0.080 N, while its weight is about 0.39 N. What is the likely result of reducing its speed?
A 0.50 kg ball on a 0.80 m string moves in a horizontal circle on a frictionless table. It completes 3.0 revolutions in 2.0 s. Calculate the tension in the string.

A 1200 kg car takes a flat circular bend of radius 50 m. On a dry road the tyres can provide a maximum friction force of 7200 N. On a wet road this maximum falls by 40%. Calculate the maximum safe speed on the wet road.
Two coins sit on a turntable rotating at 45 revolutions per minute. Coin A is 0.10 m from the centre and coin B is 0.20 m from the centre. Calculate the centripetal acceleration of coin B.

A 0.50 kg ball is swung in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m. Assume its speed is 6.0 m/s at both the top and the bottom. Calculate the tension in the string at the top of the circle. Take g = 9.8 N/kg.
A 0.20 kg bob hangs on a 1.0 m string. It moves in a horizontal circle with the string making 30° with the vertical. Calculate the time for one revolution. Take g = 9.8 N/kg.

A 0.30 kg mass is whirled on the end of a 0.60 m string in a horizontal circle on a frictionless table. The string breaks if the tension exceeds 40 N. Calculate the maximum speed the mass can have without the string breaking.

The maximum friction force between a car’s tyres and a dry flat road is 0.85 times the car’s weight. Calculate the maximum speed at which the car can take a flat bend of radius 40 m. Take g = 9.8 N/kg.
A conical pendulum has a bob on a 0.75 m string. The string makes an angle of 40° with the vertical as the bob moves in a horizontal circle. Calculate the speed of the bob. Take g = 9.8 N/kg.

A ball is swung on a string in a vertical circle of radius 0.90 m. Calculate the minimum speed it must have at the bottom of the circle for the string to stay taut all the way round. (Its speed changes as it rises: use conservation of energy.) Take g = 9.8 N/kg.

A 0.25 kg ball is swung on a string in a vertical circle of radius 0.90 m. Its speed at the bottom of the circle is 7.0 m/s. Calculate the tension in the string at the top of the circle. Take g = 9.8 N/kg.
A mass on a string is whirled round a horizontal circle at a constant speed. In which direction is the mass moving at any instant?
An object moves round a circle of radius r at a constant speed, taking a time T (the period) for each revolution. Which expression gives its speed?
An aircraft flies round a complete horizontal circle of radius 3622 m in 2.10 minutes, at a constant speed. Calculate its speed.
A referee swings her 40.0 g whistle round a horizontal circle of radius 0.500 m above her head at a constant speed, taking 1.40 s for each rotation. Calculate the speed of the whistle.
Jason stands near the edge of a merry-go-round that turns clockwise at a constant speed, as shown. What is the direction of his velocity at the instant shown?

A suitcase rides on a horizontal circular conveyor belt of radius 7.0 m that turns clockwise at a constant speed. At the instant shown the suitcase is at the right-hand side of the circle. In which direction is it moving?
The suitcase on the circular belt moves at a constant speed. Why is its motion described as accelerated?
Janet swings a ball on a string round a horizontal circle above her head at a constant speed. Which statement explains why the ball is accelerating?

Jon spins Ana round a horizontal circle on the ice, holding her by the arm. While she is still moving in the circle he lets go. Ignoring friction from the ice, how does Ana move immediately afterwards?
An object moves in a circle of radius 4.0 m at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Calculate its centripetal acceleration.
An object travelling at 6.0 m s⁻¹ moves a quarter of the way round a circle. Calculate the magnitude of its change in velocity.
A car rounds a bend of radius 25 m at a steady 10 m s⁻¹. Calculate its centripetal acceleration.

In what direction does the acceleration of an object in uniform circular motion point?

A wheel rotates at 300 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in rad s⁻¹.
An object has an angular speed of 10 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its period.
An object has an angular speed of 12.57 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its frequency of rotation.
What is the SI unit of angular speed?
Two coins sit on a turntable rotating at 45 revolutions per minute. Coin A is 0.10 m from the centre and coin B is 0.20 m from the centre. Calculate the ratio (speed of coin B) ÷ (speed of coin A).
Two coins sit on a turntable rotating at 45 revolutions per minute. Coin A is 0.10 m from the centre and coin B is 0.20 m from the centre. Calculate the centripetal acceleration of coin B.
A car of mass 1200 kg rounds a bend of radius 50 m at 15 m s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force needed.
A 0.50 kg mass moves in a circle of radius 1.2 m with angular speed 4.0 rad s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force.
A 1000 kg car rounds a bend of radius 40 m. The maximum frictional force available is 3000 N. Calculate the maximum speed before it skids.

A 0.50 kg ball is swung in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m on a string. Assume its speed is 6.0 m s⁻¹ at both the top and the bottom. Take g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹. Calculate the tension in the string at the bottom of the circle.
A 0.50 kg ball is swung in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m on a string. Take g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹. Calculate the minimum speed at the top of the circle for the string to stay taut.

An object rotates with angular speed 3.0 rad s⁻¹ at a radius of 2.0 m. Calculate its centripetal acceleration.

A satellite orbits at 7800 m s⁻¹ at a radius of 6.8 × 10⁶ m. Calculate its centripetal acceleration.
A car passes over a humpback bridge of radius 5.0 m. Calculate the speed at which it just loses contact with the road. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².

A 0.50 kg ball on a 0.80 m string moves in a horizontal circle on a frictionless table. It completes 3.0 revolutions in 2.0 s. Calculate the tension in the string.
A track is banked so that a car of any mass can round a bend of radius 80 m at 20 m s⁻¹ with no reliance on friction. Calculate the banking angle. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
A 0.50 kg ball on a string of length 1.0 m swings in a vertical circle and passes the lowest point at 4.0 m s⁻¹. Calculate the tension in the string there. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
What supplies the centripetal force keeping a satellite in orbit?

Near the Earth’s surface we use g = 9.81 N/kg. Why can’t this value be used to find the gravitational force on a satellite in a high orbit?
The Moon has a mass of 7.35 × 10²² kg and a radius of 1.74 × 10⁶ m. Calculate the gravitational field strength at its surface. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

The space shuttle and telescope orbit the Earth at a radius of 7.00 × 10⁶ m. Calculate the gravitational field strength (the acceleration due to gravity) at this height, giving your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures. Calculate the gravitational field strength due to the Earth at any point in the orbit of the ISS, 6.788 × 10⁶ m from the Earth’s centre. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and take the mass of the Earth as 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg.
Planet X has mass 4.0 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.0 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². Calculate the gravitational field strength at the surface of the planet.
Planet X has mass 4.0 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.0 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². Calculate the gravitational field strength at a height of 5.0 × 10⁶ m above the surface.

The same 2500 kg satellite orbits 4.238 × 10⁷ m from the Earth’s centre. Calculate its total energy (kinetic plus gravitational potential), including the sign. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and take the mass of the Earth as 5.98 × 10²⁴ kg.
For a satellite in a circular orbit, how is its kinetic energy Eₖ related to its gravitational potential energy Eₚ?

A 250 kg capsule of waste is released from rest at an altitude of 3.50 × 10⁵ m above the Earth’s surface. Ignoring air resistance, calculate the speed at which it would hit the Earth. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and take the Earth’s mass as 5.98 × 10²⁴ kg and its radius as 6.38 × 10⁶ m.

Does the mass of the rock affect the speed it needs to escape from the Earth?

According to Newton’s law of gravitation, the gravitational force between two point masses is…
